places.name: Tiger Hill
places.description: The most celebrated sunrise viewpoint in Darjeeling, 11km south of town at 2590m. On clear mornings (primarily Oct–Nov and Mar–Apr), the sun illuminates the Kangchenjunga massif (8586m) and, further left, Everest — the 3rd-highest and 1st-highest peaks visible from a single viewpoint. Tourists drive up in shared jeeps departing Darjeeling from 04:00. A government-run platform with a small café. Clouds frequently disappoint in monsoon and early winter; Oct–Nov gives the best odds. Entry fee applies.
places.openingDays: Daily (sunrise only; gates open before dawn)

places.name: Darjeeling Himalayan Railway
places.description: UNESCO World Heritage narrow-gauge (610mm) steam railway built 1879–1881, running 88km from New Jalpaiguri (NJP) at 116m to Darjeeling at 2204m. The locomotive, popularly called the 'Toy Train', climbs through 5 spirals and 3 reverses; the Batasia Loop is the most dramatic curve. Multiple steam and diesel services daily, including the two-hour joyride from Darjeeling to Ghoom and back. The station in Darjeeling town sits at the destination centre. One of the oldest and most scenic mountain railways in the world.
places.openingDays: Multiple daily services; timetable varies by season

places.name: Batasia Loop
places.description: Engineering marvel on the Darjeeling Himalayan Railway: a complete 360° spiral loop built to manage the 100m altitude drop from Darjeeling in a short horizontal distance. The DHR steam train circles the loop (visible from the garden above); the loop's inner garden features the Gorkha War Memorial. Panoramic views of the Kangchenjunga massif from the terrace on clear mornings. Free to walk around the garden; fee charged for the war memorial. A combined stop with the sunrise DHR joyride.

places.name: Happy Valley Tea Estate
places.description: One of the oldest tea estates in Darjeeling (est. 1854), producing first and second flush Darjeeling tea in the orthodox method. Guided tours of the factory and gardens are available during the plucking season (Mar–Nov); visitors can watch withering, rolling, oxidation, and drying. The estate is 20 minutes on foot from Chowrasta. Tea can be purchased directly from the factory. Closed Sundays and during the off-season (Dec–Feb). Entry to the factory tour is charged.

places.name: Padmaja Naidu Himalayan Zoological Park
places.description: India's highest-altitude zoo (2134m), dedicated to conservation of the Himalayan fauna. Houses the world's largest captive population of endangered snow leopards, as well as red panda, Tibetan wolf, Himalayan black bear, Himalayan salamander, and multiple pheasant species. Named after Padmaja Naidu (daughter of Sarojini Naidu, former WB governor). The zoo is also the headquarters of the Red Panda breeding programme. Separate entry from the Himalayan Mountaineering Institute next door.

places.name: Himalayan Mountaineering Institute
places.description: Premier mountaineering institute founded 1954 by the Indian government and Tenzing Norgay, within a year of the first ascent of Everest. Tenzing Norgay directed the institute for 22 years. The Everest Museum within the institute houses artefacts from early Himalayan expeditions including gear from the 1953 Everest climb. Basic and advanced mountaineering courses are offered. The museum is open to visitors with a combined ticket shared with the zoo. A significant heritage site for Himalayan climbing history.
places.area: Birch Hill, Darjeeling (shared campus with Padmaja Naidu Zoo)

places.name: Ghoom Monastery (Yiga Choeling Gompa)
places.description: The oldest Tibetan Buddhist monastery in Darjeeling district (built 1875), enshrining a 5-metre clay statue of Maitreya (the Future Buddha), one of the most sacred in the Darjeeling hills. The monastery belongs to the Yellow Hat (Gelugpa) sect and houses resident monks. Located in Ghoom village, 8km south of Darjeeling, on the DHR joyride route (Ghoom Station is 200m away). A calm, authentic Tibetan monastery atmosphere; morning prayers can be attended respectfully.

places.name: Peace Pagoda Darjeeling
places.description: Japanese Nipponzan-Myohoji Buddhist peace pagoda, one of dozens built globally by the order after World War II. Set on a hilltop at Jalapahar with views over Darjeeling and the plains. The white-painted pagoda enshrines a gilded Buddha statue on each of its four faces. Reachable by road or a steep 30-minute climb from the town side. Free to visit. Quiet atmosphere; fewer crowds than the main ridge attractions.

places.name: Observatory Hill (Mahakal Temple)
places.description: Sacred hilltop at the highest point within Darjeeling town, associated with both Hindu and Buddhist traditions. The hilltop housed the original Bhutia Buddhist monastery before Darjeeling was established; it is now shared by a Hindu shrine (Mahakal/Shiva), prayer flags, and a small Bhutia monastery. The summit provides the best in-town views of the Kangchenjunga range. Sacred to the local Lepcha, Bhutia, and Gorkha communities. Free to climb; 15-minute walk from Chowrasta.

places.name: Lloyd Botanical Garden
places.description: Botanical garden established 1878, named after William Lloyd who donated the land. The garden houses over 2000 species of Himalayan flora including orchids, rhododendrons, ferns, and medicinal plants. The orchid house is particularly notable. One of the oldest botanical gardens in the Eastern Himalayas. Located just below Darjeeling town, a short walk from Chowrasta. Free to enter. At its best in spring (Mar–May) during rhododendron and orchid bloom.

places.name: Chowrasta Mall
places.description: Darjeeling's main pedestrian square and social hub, at the junction of four pedestrianised streets (the name means 'four roads'). Pony rides, chess tables, musicians, and vendors selling Darjeeling tea and momos make this the living heart of the town. Surrounded by colonial-era buildings. The most photogenic backdrop for the Kangchenjunga sunrise view from town — when clear, the massif is visible to the northwest. Evening is lively with locals and tourists; free to stroll. The adjacent roads lead to the Oxford Bookshop and the Planters' Club.

places.name: Darjeeling Ropeway
places.description: Government-operated cable car running from the Singamari station near Darjeeling to Tukvar Tea Estate in the valley, dropping roughly 600m over 1.8km. One of the oldest operating ropeways in India. Provides aerial views over the tea gardens and Darjeeling hillside. Operational schedule can be irregular; confirm on the day. Entry fee charged; may be crowded during peak season.
places.openingDays: Daily 08:00–16:00 (check day of; schedule can vary)
